title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover compaction heuristics v14
author: Asha Patel
ci_checks: integration: pass (reran flaky test kv_cache_integration::paging_repro on second run)
description:
Context: Production bundles with long-tail sequence distributions were seeing elevated memory fragmentation and excessive spill-to-disk during bursty traffic. Previous heuristics (v11-v13) improved average cost but left corner-cases where small hot keys caused repeated tiny spills and compaction churn, increasing tail latency and I/O. Motivation: Reduce tail latency and unnecessary disk churn by making eviction decisions aware of fragmentation, per-key allocation patterns, and a light-weight compaction budget.

What this PR does: Introduces v14 of the KV cache memory management strategy with three coordinated changes: (1) adaptive eviction priority that combines recency, per-key fragmentation score, and estimated resident size to avoid repeatedly evicting hot but fragmented entries; (2) spillover compaction windows that batch small spill events into a single compaction job when beneficial, rather than immediate synchronous spills; (3) a light-weight in-memory coalescing pass that defers tiny free regions and triggers opportunistic compaction during low-load windows.

Design details: - Eviction scoring: new EvictionScore = alpha*LRU_rank + beta*FragmentationScore + gamma*size_factor. Coefficients are runtime-configurable and default to values tuned from production traces. FragmentationScore is computed by sampling allocation vectors per-key and normalizing by a sliding-window of allocations to keep compute cheap. - Spill compaction windows: small spill events (< 4MB) are queued for up to 200ms to allow coalescing; if queue grows or memory pressure increases, a compaction job runs earlier. This avoids issuing frequent small disk writes and amortizes IOPS. - Opportunistic compaction: when GPU/serving threads are idle (detected by existing scheduler hooks), a background compaction worker runs one slice of compaction work bounded by time budget to reduce fragmentation without impacting latency SLOs. - Backwards compatibility: new behavior is behind a feature flag kv.eviction.adaptive_v14 and defaults to ON for new clusters; rollout plan includes Canary on 10% of Dedicated nodes, then 50%, then global.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks on r5/g5 clusters using production-sampled trace: - 95th token latency: -12% (reduction) - 99th token latency: -18% - Disk write ops during burst window: -40% - Average CPU overhead per serving thread: +1.8% (within budget) Tail-case test with heavy small-key churn: spill events reduced by 3.1x.

Files changed (high-level): runtime/kv_cache/{eviction.rs, compaction.rs, allocator.rs}, runtime/scheduler/idle_hook.rs, configs/kv_defaults.toml, tests/kv_eviction_integration.rs, docs/kv-cache/eviction.md.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for new scoring and sampling added. - Integration test kv_cache_integration::paging_repro added to reproduce prior regression and assert reduced spill events. - End-to-end benchmarks run in perf-canary with simulated burst traces. - Observability: added metrics kv.evictions.{by_reason,fragmentation_score} and kv.compaction.{queued_jobs,run_duration_ms} so ops can validate behavior.

Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature flag in Canary (10%) for 72 hours with alerting on kv.compaction.run_duration_ms and disk.write_ops; 2) If stable, expand to 50% for 7 days and compare cost/latency dashboards; 3) Full deployment and remove feature flag after 30 days if no regressions.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps compaction CPU budget conservative to avoid interfering with serving threads. Further tuning (v15) will explore adaptive budget based on real-time utilization.

review_comments: Ben Carter: Can we make the compaction window configurable per-customer? Some Dedicated deployments have very low IOPS limits.
Asha Patel (author): Added a runtime config kv.compaction.window_ms and documented recommended values. Default remains 200ms.
Li Wei: FragmentationScore sampling looks potentially expensive on hot keys. Can we sample less frequently or use an exponential backoff when a key is hot?
Asha Patel: We use a sliding reservoir sampler capped at 10 samples/sec per key and exponential backoff when access frequency exceeds threshold. Added tests and comments.
Sofia Martinez: Observability looks good. Please add an alert for compaction.run_duration_ms exceeding 500ms.
Asha Patel: Added alerting recommendation to docs and created Linear task ENG-3320 to hook into AlertManager.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: adaptive eviction that reduces tail latency, batched spillover compaction to lower disk churn, and opportunistic compaction to reduce fragmentation. Enabled behind feature flag kv.eviction.adaptive_v14; rollout controlled by Canary/Gradual deploy.
